title: Principality of Upper Hungary
capsule: The Principality of Upper Hungary was an Ottoman-vassal buffer state established in 1682 under Imre Thököly, a Hungarian Protestant noble who led the kuruc rebellion against Habsburg rule and received the title from the Ottoman sultan after his forces seized northern Hungary. At its maximum extent Thököly controlled a strip of Royal Hungary north of the Danube from Kassa (Košice) to the Carpathians. The Ottoman defeat at the Battle of Vienna (September 1683) and the subsequent Holy League offensive rapidly eroded his position; Thököly lost Kassa in 1685 and the Habsburgs extinguished the principality by 1687, reducing him to a Turkish pensioner in exile at Izmit, where he died in 1705. The entity represents the last Ottoman-sponsored attempt to establish a client Hungarian polity within the kingdom.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The political history is well documented in Habsburg and Ottoman sources, but the exact territorial boundaries shifted month to month during the 1683–1687 conflict and cartographic precision is limited.
